unit_label: BRBL C U02 MSMED Act: Apply audited-buyer disclosures, interest disallowance and offence-specific penalties

facts.statement: Audited buyers disclose specified principal and interest amounts, including unpaid and further interest. Section 23 disallows the Act interest deduction; section 24 overrides inconsistent laws for sections 15-23. Intentional section 8(1)/26(2) offences differ from buyer section 22 contravention fine (at least 10000).

facts.locator: printed pp.233-242 / PDF pp.252-261, whole unit and end questions visually inspected
facts.statement: The chapter covers this objective, but its older classification values and historical memorandum treatment must be read with the retained notifications.

payload.title: Paying principal does not make the interest trail disappear
payload.core_explanation_md:
For a buyer whose annual accounts must be audited under a law, section 22 requires the specified principal and interest disclosures, including separate year-end unpaid amounts and delayed-payment/further-interest information. A nil principal balance is not enough to conclude that no MSMED disclosure or unpaid interest remains.

Section 23 disallows deduction of interest payable or paid under the Act for income-tax computation. This card does not determine every tax consequence of the purchase principal. Section 24 gives sections 15-23 overriding effect over inconsistent laws. The penalty route also matters: section 27 distinguishes intentional section 8(1)/26(2) contraventions from an audited buyer breach of section 22, for which the stated fine is at least INR 10,000. Do not transpose the first-offence INR 1,000 ceiling to that separate buyer offence.

self_check.prompt_text: Does clearing principal necessarily clear statutory interest and all disclosure obligations?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Reconcile the interest and the statutory disclosure categories separately.

payload.stem_md: An audited buyer pays the invoice principal after delay but leaves statutory interest unpaid. Which year-end approach fits section 22?

options.text_md: Reconcile and disclose the applicable unpaid interest and other specified delay information
options.explanation_md: Payment of principal does not erase the distinct interest disclosure requirements.

options.text_md: Delete the supplier record because principal is nil
options.explanation_md: The interest trail may remain even when principal has been paid.

options.text_md: Deduct every statutory interest charge because all business interest is deductible
options.explanation_md: Section 23 specifically disallows the interest under this Act.

options.text_md: Treat unpaid interest as an automatic waiver by the supplier
options.explanation_md: Nonpayment is not evidence of an agreed or legally effective waiver.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Payment of principal does not erase the distinct interest disclosure requirements.

payload.stem_md: A training note applies the INR 1,000 first-conviction ceiling to a buyer contravention of section 22. What is wrong with that comparison?

options.text_md: All offences under the Act carry the same ceiling
options.explanation_md: Section 27 distinguishes the types of contravention.

options.text_md: Section 22 concerns only voluntary unaudited accounts
options.explanation_md: It addresses buyers whose annual accounts must be audited by law.

options.text_md: The statutory interest is a payment to the Government
options.explanation_md: The delayed-payment interest is owed to the supplier, not a tax payment.

options.text_md: Buyer contravention of section 22 has a separate fine of at least INR 10,000
options.explanation_md: The first-conviction ceiling belongs to the specified intentional section 8/26 offence, not this offence.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The first-conviction ceiling belongs to the specified intentional section 8/26 offence, not this offence.
